AIID-103.title: Twitter’s Image Cropping Tool Allegedly Showed Gender and Racial Bias
AIID-103.summary: Twitter's saliency-based image cropping algorithm was found to exhibit racial and gender biases, consistently favoring white and lighter-skinned individuals over Black individuals in photo previews. Further research identified additional harms, including the marginalization of elderly people and individuals with disabilities, as well as biases related to language and beauty filters. In response, Twitter conducted internal audits, open-sourced their analysis, launched an algorithmic bias bounty program, and eventually moved away from automated cropping in favor of user-controlled image display.
AIID-103.description: Twitter's photo cropping algorithm was revealed by researchers to favor white and women faces in photos containing multiple faces, prompting the company to stop its use on mobile platform.
AIID-103.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"1.1 Unfair discrimination and misrepresentation","justification":"The automated cropping caused representational harm by denying users the ability to represent themselves as they wished on the platform."}]
AIID-103.domainJustification: The image-cropping algorithm performed with unequal accuracy and effectiveness across different demographic groups, systematically favoring lighter-skinned individuals over Black individuals.
AIID-103.allegedHarmedParties: Twitter Users, Twitter non-white users, Twitter non-male users
AIID-103.aiGoalJustification: The primary function of the algorithm was to automatically crop images to focus on the most salient parts for timeline previews.

AIID-104.title: California's Algorithm Considered ZIP Codes in Vaccine Distribution, Allegedly Excluding Low-Income Neighborhoods and Communities of Color
AIID-104.summary: An analysis of California's COVID-19 vaccine distribution algorithm revealed that using ZIP codes instead of census tracts to allocate supply likely excluded over 2 million people in high-need, underserved neighborhoods. The algorithm, built by Blue Shield, prioritized larger geographic areas, which critics argue masked the needs of specific low-income census tracts and disproportionately impacted Black and Latinx populations.
AIID-104.description: California's vaccine-distribution algorithm used ZIP codes as opposed to census tracts in its decision-making, which critics said undermined equity and access for vulnerable communities who are largely low-income, underserved neighborhoods with low Healthy Places Index scores.
AIID-104.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"7.3 Lack of capability or robustness","justification":"The algorithm lacked the geographic resolution (robustness) to accurately identify vulnerable pockets within larger ZIP codes, leading to system failure in critical resource allocation."}]
AIID-104.domainJustification: The vaccine distribution algorithm's effectiveness in prioritizing high-need areas was significantly lower for communities of color, resulting in unequal outcomes and reduced benefits for Latinx and Black populations.
AIID-104.allegedHarmedParties: California low-income neighborhoods, California communities of color
AIID-104.aiGoalJustification: The primary goal of the Blue Shield algorithm was to allocate scarce COVID-19 vaccine resources across different geographic regions in California.

AIID-105.title: Tesla Model 3 on Autopilot Crashed into a Ford Explorer Pickup, Killing a Fifteen-Year-Old in California
AIID-105.summary: In August 2019, a Tesla Model 3 operating on Autopilot crashed into a Ford Explorer on a California freeway. Data and video from the vehicle indicated that the system failed to slow down until a fraction of a second before impact. The collision resulted in the death of a fifteen-year-old passenger, Jovani Maldonado. The incident has led to a lawsuit and raised concerns regarding the safety, monitoring, and performance of Tesla's Autopilot system.
AIID-105.description: A Tesla Model 3 on Autopilot mode crashed into a pickup on a California freeway, where data and video from the company showed neither Autopilot nor the driver slowing the vehicle until seconds before the crash.
AIID-105.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"5.1 Overreliance and unsafe use","justification":"The report highlights that Tesla's weak driver-monitoring system allows or encourages drivers to overrely on Autopilot, leading to inattention."}]
AIID-105.domainJustification: The primary failure was the Autopilot system's inability to detect and brake for a slowing vehicle in front of it, representing a lack of capability or robustness in real-world driving conditions.
AIID-105.allegedHarmedParties: Jovani Maldonado, California public, Benjamin Maldonado

AIID-106.title: Korean Chatbot Luda Made Offensive Remarks towards Minority Groups
AIID-106.summary: The AI chatbot 'Luda', developed by South Korean startup Scatter Lab, was suspended shortly after its December 2020 launch due to generating hate speech, discriminatory remarks, and sexually explicit content. The incident revealed that the model was trained on private KakaoTalk conversation data harvested from the company's other apps without user consent. This resulted in significant privacy breaches, including the exposure of personal information, and led to government investigations, class-action lawsuits, and a monetary penalty against the developer.
AIID-106.description: A Korean interactive chatbot was shown in screenshots to have used derogatory and bigoted language when asked about lesbians, Black people, and people with disabilities.
AIID-106.subdomain: 2.1 Compromise of privacy by obtaining, leaking or correctly inferring sensitive information

AIID-106.domainJustification: The primary harm and legal sanctions stemmed from the AI system leaking non-public sensitive information (names, addresses, bank accounts) harvested from private KakaoTalk logs without consent.
AIID-106.allegedHarmedParties: Korean people with disabilities, Korean people of gender minorities, Korean Facebook Messenger users
AIID-106.aiGoalJustification: The AI system was explicitly developed and deployed as an open-domain conversational chatbot designed to simulate a 20-year-old female college student.

AIID-108.title: Skating Rink’s Facial Recognition Cameras Misidentified Black Teenager as Banned Troublemaker

AIID-109.title: PimEyes's Facial Recognition AI Allegedly Lacked Safeguards to Prevent Itself from Being Abused
AIID-109.summary: PimEyes is a subscription-based facial recognition search engine that allows users to upload a photo and find other images of that person across the internet. Critics and researchers argue the tool lacks sufficient safeguards, enabling stalking, harassment, and the creation of non-consensual dossiers on individuals. Despite the company's claims that it is intended for self-monitoring, the lack of effective oversight has led to widespread misuse by anonymous users on forums like 4chan.

AIID-110.title: Arkansas's Opaque Algorithm to Allocate Health Care Excessively Cut Down Hours for Beneficiaries
AIID-110.summary: In 2016, the Arkansas Department of Human Services implemented an algorithmic tool designed by InterRAI to allocate home care hours for Medicaid beneficiaries. The system, implemented by a third-party vendor, contained significant coding errors regarding diabetes and cerebral palsy, leading to drastic and unexplained reductions in care hours for hundreds of disabled individuals. A federal lawsuit revealed these flaws, highlighting the lack of transparency and the inability of beneficiaries to effectively challenge automated decisions.
AIID-110.description: Beneficiaries of the Arkansas Department of Human Services (DHS)'s Medicaid waiver program were allocated excessively fewer hours of caretaker visit via an algorithm deployed to boost efficiency, which reportedly contained errors and whose outputs varied wildly despite small input changes.

AIID-114.title: Amazon's Rekognition Falsely Matched Members of Congress to Mugshots

AIID-115.title: Genderify’s AI to Predict a Person’s Gender Revealed by Free API Users to Exhibit Bias
AIID-115.summary: Genderify was an AI-powered service that attempted to predict gender from names, emails, and usernames. Following its launch, users discovered the system was riddled with sexist stereotypes, such as associating professional titles like 'doctor' with men and 'nurse' with women, while also enforcing a harmful gender binary. Due to significant public backlash regarding these biases and the potential for discriminatory outcomes in marketing and employment, the company shut down the service shortly after its release.
AIID-115.description: A company's AI predicting a person's gender based on their name, email address, or username was reported by its users to show biased and inaccurate results.

AIID-115.aiGoalJustification: The primary goal of the AI system was Gender Identification, as it was designed to identify a person's gender by analyzing their name, username, or email address. A secondary goal was Marketing Analytics Generation, as it was pitched to help businesses segment marketing databases and obtain demographic statistics.

AIID-116.title: Amazon's AI Cameras Incorrectly Penalized Delivery Drivers for Mistakes They Did Not Make
AIID-116.summary: Amazon deployed Netradyne AI-powered cameras in its delivery fleet to monitor driver safety and performance. Drivers and delivery partners report that the system frequently generates false positive 'events'—such as misidentifying yield signs as stop signs or flagging safe driving maneuvers as distractions—which negatively impact performance scores. These erroneous scores result in financial losses for delivery companies and the loss of bonuses for drivers, creating a high-pressure environment that has led some drivers to attempt to circumvent the surveillance.

AIID-117.title: TikTok's "Suggested Accounts" Algorithm Allegedly Reinforced Racial Bias through Feedback Loops
AIID-117.summary: Researcher Marc Faddoul observed that TikTok's 'Suggested Accounts' feature recommended users who physically resembled the accounts he initially followed, such as race, age, and gender. While TikTok attributed these results to collaborative filtering based on user behavior, Faddoul raised concerns that such mechanisms create feedback loops that marginalize creators from underrepresented groups. The incident highlights the potential for recommendation algorithms to reinforce societal biases and create 'filter bubbles' even without explicit intent to discriminate.

AIID-118.title: OpenAI's GPT-3 Associated Muslims with Violence
AIID-118.summary: Researchers discovered that OpenAI's GPT-3 model exhibits persistent and severe anti-Muslim bias, frequently associating the term 'Muslim' with violence, terrorism, and extremist propaganda. The model was found to generate novel bigotry statements and repeat pro-China propaganda regarding the treatment of Uyghur Muslims. This incident highlights the risks of deploying large-scale language models trained on unvetted internet data, which can automate and amplify societal prejudices.

AIID-119.title: Xsolla Employees Fired by CEO Allegedly via Big Data Analytics of Work Activities

AIID-123.title: Epic Systems’s Sepsis Prediction Algorithms Revealed to Have High Error Rates on Seriously Ill Patients
AIID-123.summary: An independent study of the Epic Sepsis Model (ESM) at Michigan Medicine revealed that the tool significantly underperformed compared to vendor claims. The study found the model missed 67% of sepsis cases and produced a high rate of false positives, leading to alert fatigue among clinicians. This incident highlights the risks of deploying proprietary, non-validated AI models in critical clinical settings.

AIID-124.title: Optum Algorithmic Health Risk Scores Reportedly Underestimated Black Patients' Needs
AIID-124.summary: A widely used health-care algorithm developed by Optum was found to systematically disadvantage Black patients by using health-care costs as a proxy for medical need. Because historical systemic factors resulted in lower spending on Black patients, the algorithm incorrectly assigned them lower risk scores, effectively excluding them from programs providing extra medical support. The study highlighted how race-neutral metrics can perpetuate racial bias when applied to data reflecting existing societal inequalities.
AIID-124.description: Researchers analyzing an Optum algorithm used by a large academic hospital reportedly found evidence that it tended to under-predict the health care needs of Black patients, which in turn appeared to result in lower prioritization for extra care programs compared with white patients exhibiting similar health profiles.

AIID-125.title: Amazon’s Robotic Fulfillment Centers Have Higher Serious Injury Rates
AIID-125.summary: Internal Amazon records reveal that the company's robotic fulfillment centers have significantly higher serious injury rates compared to traditional sites. The robots enabled increased production quotas, forcing workers to perform repetitive motions at higher speeds, which resulted in a mounting injury crisis. Despite public claims that robots make jobs safer, internal data shows injury rates rose consistently between 2016 and 2019, particularly during peak shopping periods.

AIID-131.title: Proctoring Algorithm in Online California Bar Exam Flagged an Unusually High Number of Alleged Cheaters
AIID-131.summary: During the October 2020 California bar exam, an AI-powered proctoring system flagged over one-third of the 9,301 test-takers for alleged rule violations. This high rate of flagging led to widespread accusations of cheating, forcing many applicants to undergo a stressful review process to prove their innocence. Critics and legal representatives argued that the system was overly sensitive and that the process for challenging these allegations was opaque and unfair, as applicants were often denied access to the video evidence used against them.
AIID-131.description: The proctoring algorithm used in a California bar exam cited a third of thousands of applicants as cheaters, resulting in allegations where exam takers were instructed to prove otherwise without seeing their incriminating video evidence.
AIID-131.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"1.3 Unequal performance across groups","justification":"The reports note that the algorithm flagged Black and other minority applicants for merely existing, indicating potential demographic bias and unequal performance."},{"code":"5.1 Overreliance and unsafe use","justification":"The bar examiners over-relied on the AI's automated flags, issuing violation notices to thousands of applicants without first conducting human verification of the video evidence."}]
AIID-131.domainJustification: The AI proctoring software failed to perform reliably under normal test-taking conditions, resulting in an extremely high false-positive rate where 34% of innocent applicants were flagged for cheating.
AIID-131.allegedDeployer: California Bar’s Committee of Bar Examiners
AIID-131.allegedHarmedParties: flagged California bar exam takers, California bar exam takers
AIID-131.aiGoalJustification: The AI system was explicitly designed and deployed to monitor test-takers via webcam and microphone to detect and flag potential cheating behaviors during the online bar exam.

AIID-132.title: TikTok’s Content Moderation Allegedly Failed to Adequately Take down Videos Promoting Eating Disorders
AIID-132.summary: TikTok's recommendation algorithm has been found to distribute content promoting eating disorders to its users, including those who have not actively sought out such material. Despite the platform's efforts to ban specific hashtags, users have successfully bypassed these restrictions using misspellings. The algorithm's engagement-based design creates a cycle that can trap vulnerable users in exposure to harmful content, raising significant concerns regarding the platform's safety procedures.
AIID-132.description: Videos promoting eating disorders evaded TikTok's automated violation detection system without difficulty via common misspellings of search terms, bypassing its ban of violating hashtags such as "proana" and "anorexia".

AIID-136.title: Brand Safety Tech Firms Falsely Claimed Use of AI, Blocking Ads Using Simple Keyword Lists
AIID-136.summary: Brand safety technology firms marketed their products as utilizing advanced AI and machine learning to protect advertisers, but in practice, these systems relied on rudimentary keyword lists. This resulted in the systematic misclassification of legitimate news articles as 'unsafe' due to the presence of benign words like 'death' or 'weapons' in news contexts. Consequently, mainstream publishers suffered significant ad revenue losses, while ad budgets were inadvertently diverted to lower-quality sites.

AIID-139.title: Amazon’s Search and Recommendation Algorithms Found by Auditors to Have Boosted Products That Contained Vaccine Misinformation
AIID-139.summary: Researchers conducted a systematic audit of Amazon's search and recommendation algorithms and discovered that they amplify vaccine misinformation. The study found that 10.47% of search results for vaccine-related queries promoted misinformative products, which were often ranked higher than debunking content. Additionally, the researchers identified a 'filter-bubble' effect where user interaction with misinformative products led to further recommendations of similar misinformation.

AIID-141.title: California Police Turned on Music to Allegedly Trigger Instagram’s DCMA to Avoid Being Live-Streamed
AIID-141.summary: Beverly Hills police officers were observed playing copyrighted music during interactions with an activist, Sennett Devermont, who was livestreaming the encounters on Instagram. AIID-144.title: YouTube's AI Mistakenly Banned Chess Channel over Chess Language Misinterpretation
AIID-144.summary: In June 2020, the YouTube channel of popular chess creator Agadmator was blocked for 24 hours after the platform's automated hate speech detection system flagged his content. Researchers from Carnegie Mellon University investigated the incident and concluded that the AI likely misinterpreted common chess terminology—such as 'black', 'white', 'attack', and 'threat'—as racist language. The incident highlights the limitations of automated moderation systems when applied to specialized contexts without sufficient training data.

AIID-145.title: Tesla's Autopilot Misidentified the Moon as Yellow Stop Light
AIID-145.summary: Tesla's Autopilot and Full Self-Driving (FSD) systems have been documented repeatedly misidentifying objects such as the moon, billboards, and signs as traffic signals. Despite Tesla's marketing, the FSD software remains in beta and requires constant human intervention to prevent collisions and erratic driving behavior.

AIID-146.title: Research Prototype AI, Delphi, Reportedly Gave Racially Biased Answers on Ethics
AIID-146.summary: Delphi, a research prototype AI from the Allen Institute for AI, was released to provide moral judgments on ethical dilemmas. The system quickly went viral for generating offensive, racist, and homophobic content, as well as condoning harmful behaviors based on user-provided framing. The incident highlights the risks of deploying models trained on internet-scraped data without sufficient safeguards for moral reasoning.

AIID-147.title: Reported AI-Cloned Voice Used to Deceive Hong Kong Bank Manager in Purported $35 Million Fraud Scheme
AIID-147.summary: In January 2020, a bank manager in Hong Kong was defrauded of $35 million after receiving phone calls and emails from individuals impersonating his company's director and a lawyer. The fraudsters utilized AI-based voice cloning technology to mimic the director's voice, successfully convincing the manager to authorize large wire transfers to various international accounts. The incident, which involved at least 17 individuals, is currently under investigation by authorities in the UAE and the United States.
AIID-147.description: In January 2020, a Hong Kong-based bank manager for a Japanese company reportedly authorized $35 million in transfers after receiving a call from someone whose voice matched the company director's. According to Emirati investigators, scammers used AI-based voice cloning to impersonate the executive. The fraud allegedly involved at least 17 individuals and reportedly led to global fund transfers that triggered a UAE investigation. U.S. authorities were reportedly later asked to help trace part of the funds sent to U.S. banks.
AIID-147.domainJustification: The incident involved fraudsters using AI voice-cloning technology to impersonate a company director and execute a targeted financial scam, resulting in a $35 million loss.

AIID-148.title: Web Accessibility Vendors Allegedly Falsely Claimed to Provide Compliance Using AI
AIID-148.summary: This report documents allegations of widespread deceptive marketing by vendors of AI-powered web accessibility 'overlay' products. AIID-149.title: Zillow Shut Down Zillow Offers Division Allegedly Due to Predictive Pricing Tool's Insufficient Accuracy
AIID-149.summary: Zillow shut down its 'Zillow Offers' iBuying division after its 'Zestimate' machine-learning algorithm failed to accurately predict home prices in a volatile market. The company purchased thousands of homes at prices higher than their resale value, resulting in a $540 million write-down and the layoff of 25% of its workforce. The incident highlights the risks of deploying predictive AI models for high-stakes, real-world financial decisions.
AIID-149.description: Zillow's AI-powered predictive pricing tool Zestimate was allegedly not able to accurately forecast housing prices three to six months in advance due to rapid market changes, prompting division shutdown and layoff of a few thousand employees.

AIID-149.domainJustification: The Zestimate algorithm failed to perform robustly under volatile market conditions, leading to highly inaccurate home price predictions that caused severe financial losses.
AIID-149.aiGoalJustification: The Zestimate algorithm's primary function is to estimate the market value of residential properties based on historical and current real estate data, which was then used to forecast future prices for Zillow's iBuying business.

AIID-150.title: Swedish Contraceptive App, Natural Cycles, Allegedly Failed to Correctly Map Menstrual Cycle
AIID-150.summary: The Natural Cycles contraceptive app faced scrutiny after users reported unwanted pregnancies, leading to an investigation by the Swedish Medical Products Agency. The app, which uses an algorithm to predict fertility based on basal body temperature, was criticized for its effectiveness and the potential for user error. While the company maintains the app is effective when used correctly, reports of failures prompted concerns about its reliability as a primary method of birth control.
AIID-150.description: Some women using the contraceptive app, Natural Cycles, reported unwanted pregnancies, revealing its algorithm's difficulties in mapping menstrual cycles.
AIID-150.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"5.1 Overreliance and unsafe use","justification":"Users placed a high level of trust in the app, treating it with the same expectations as a contraceptive pill, which led to unsafe reliance in a critical health scenario."}]
AIID-150.domainJustification: The algorithm lacked the robustness to handle typical human variations, such as irregular menstrual cycles, stress, or minor temperature tracking errors, leading to incorrect fertility predictions.
AIID-150.aiGoalJustification: The primary goal of the Natural Cycles algorithm is to act as a health assistant that tracks and analyzes basal body temperature to predict fertility windows and assist with contraception.

AIID-151.title: California Regulator Suspended Pony.ai's Driverless Testing Permit Following a Non-Fatal Collision
AIID-151.summary: On October 28, 2021, a Pony.ai autonomous vehicle collided with a center divider and traffic sign in Fremont, California, while performing a lane change in autonomous mode. The incident resulted in moderate vehicle damage and no injuries. Following the crash, the California DMV suspended Pony.ai's driverless testing permit, and the NHTSA subsequently requested a recall of the software, marking the first-ever recall of an automated driving system.

AIID-152.title: SoftBank's Humanoid Robot, Pepper, Reportedly Frequently Made Errors, Prompting Dismissal
AIID-152.summary: SoftBank's Pepper robot, marketed as a sophisticated humanoid assistant, failed to meet performance expectations across various sectors including funeral services, nursing homes, and banking. Users reported frequent mechanical breakdowns, inability to recognize faces, and limited functionality, resulting in contract terminations and financial losses for businesses and individuals. The product line was eventually discontinued as simpler, more reliable alternatives like smart speakers proved more effective.

AIID-154.title: Justice Department’s Recidivism Risk Algorithm PATTERN Allegedly Caused Persistent Disparities Along Racial Lines
AIID-154.summary: The Department of Justice's PATTERN recidivism risk assessment tool was found to produce racially biased results, leading to the misclassification of thousands of inmates. AIID-161.title: Facebook's Ad Delivery Reportedly Excluded Audience along Racial and Gender Lines
AIID-161.summary: Independent audits of Facebook's ad-delivery system revealed that its algorithms were skewing the delivery of housing and employment advertisements along gender and racial lines. Despite Facebook's claims of taking steps to address discrimination, researchers found that the system continued to reproduce demographic skews even when advertisers used neutral targeting parameters. This behavior resulted in disparate exposure to job and housing opportunities, raising significant concerns regarding algorithmic fairness and compliance with equal employment opportunity laws.

AIID-162.title: ETS Used Allegedly Flawed Voice Recognition Evidence to Accuse and Assess Scale of Cheating, Causing Thousands to be Deported from the UK
AIID-162.summary: Following a 2014 fraud investigation, ETS provided the UK Home Office with voice recognition analysis to identify cheating on TOEIC exams. The Home Office used this data to revoke visas and deport thousands of students. Subsequent investigations revealed the voice recognition evidence was deeply flawed, with many innocent individuals wrongly accused and deported without due process.
AIID-162.description: International testing organization ETS admits voice recognition as evidence of cheating for thousands of previous TOEIC test-takers that reportedly included wrongfully accused people, causing them to be deported without an appeal process or seeing their incriminating evidence.
AIID-162.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"5.1 Overreliance and unsafe use","justification":"The UK Home Office totally relied on the unverified and flawed AI outputs to take severe immigration enforcement actions without human verification."}]
AIID-162.domainJustification: The AI system failed to perform reliably, generating massive false-positive rates due to technical flaws like mismatched voice files and vulnerability to remote testing manipulation.
AIID-162.allegedHarmedParties: UK Home Office, UK ETS test takers, UK ETS past test takers
AIID-162.aiGoalJustification: The system's primary function was voice recognition to identify if the same voice appeared on multiple test recordings, which was used for cheating detection.

AIID-163.title: Facebook’s Hate Speech Detection Algorithms Allegedly Disproportionately Failed to Remove Racist Content towards Minority Groups
AIID-163.summary: Internal Facebook documents revealed that the company's hate speech detection algorithms were ineffective at removing severe, targeted hate speech against minority groups, while simultaneously over-indexing on less harmful content. Despite internal research identifying these failures and proposing an overhaul to better protect vulnerable groups, executives rejected the changes to maintain a 'politically neutral' appearance. This resulted in a platform environment where minority users, particularly Black users, faced disproportionate exposure to racist and derogatory language.
AIID-163.description: Facebook’s hate-speech detection algorithms was found by company researchers to have under-reported less common but more harmful content that was more often experienced by minority groups such as Black, Muslim, LGBTQ, and Jewish users.

AIID-163.allegedHarmedParties: Facebook users of minority groups, Facebook users
AIID-163.aiGoalJustification: The AI system's primary goal was to detect and automatically remove hate speech on the Facebook platform.

AIID-164.title: Facebook "News Feed" Allegedly Boosted Misinformation and Violating Content Following Use of MSI Metric
AIID-164.summary: In early 2018, Facebook overhauled its News Feed algorithm to prioritize 'meaningful social interactions' (MSI) by heavily weighting reshares and comments. Internal research subsequently revealed that this change incentivized the creation and spread of sensationalist, toxic, and misinformative content, as such material generated higher engagement. Despite warnings from staff that the platform was becoming an 'angrier place' and harming democratic discourse, leadership resisted broad fixes due to concerns about potential declines in user engagement metrics.
AIID-164.description: After the “News Feed” algorithm had been overhauled to boost engagement between friends and family in early 2018, its heavy weighting of re-shared content was alleged found by company researchers to have pushed content creators to reorient their posts towards outrage and sensationalism, causing a proliferation of misinformation, toxicity, and violent content.

AIID-165.title: Image Upscaling Algorithm PULSE Allegedly Produced Facial Images with Caucasian Features More Often
AIID-165.summary: The PULSE image upscaling algorithm, powered by NVIDIA's StyleGAN, was found to exhibit significant racial bias by consistently generating Caucasian-looking faces when provided with low-resolution inputs of people of color. Researchers and academics engaged in a public debate regarding whether this bias originated from the training dataset or the model's selection algorithm, highlighting broader concerns about systemic bias in AI development and the lack of diversity among researchers.
AIID-165.description: Image upscaling tool PULSE powered by NVIDIA's StyleGAN reportedly generated faces with Caucasian features more often, although AI academics, engineers, and researchers were not in agreement about where the source of bias was.
AIID-165.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"1.1 Unfair discrimination and misrepresentation","justification":"The system misrepresents individuals of color by generating white faces from their pixelated images, reinforcing racial biases."}]
AIID-165.domainJustification: The upscaling algorithm performs with significantly lower accuracy and effectiveness for people of color compared to white individuals, resulting in unequal outcomes.
AIID-165.aiGoalJustification: The primary function of the PULSE algorithm is to perform super-resolution upscaling on low-resolution images by generating realistic high-resolution faces using StyleGAN.

AIID-166.title: Networking Platform Giggle Employs AI to Determine Users’ Gender, Allegedly Excluding Transgender Women
AIID-166.summary: The social networking app Giggle utilized Kairos facial recognition software to perform gender verification on new users. The system faced significant criticism for discriminatory performance, specifically failing to accurately classify women of color, and was used by the platform's founder to exclude transgender women. The app also faced scrutiny for its extensive data collection practices and privacy policies.
AIID-166.description: A social networking platform, Giggle, allegedly collected, shared to third-parties, and used sensitive information and biometric data to verify whether a person is a woman via facial recognition, which critics claimed to be discriminatory against women of color and harmful towards trans women.

AIID-166.domainJustification: The facial recognition software exhibited unequal performance across demographic groups, specifically misclassifying darker-skinned women at a much higher rate of 22.5% and failing to verify transgender women.
AIID-166.aiGoalJustification: The primary function of the Kairos AI integration in the Giggle app was to analyze selfies to identify the gender of users for verification purposes.

AIID-167.title: Researchers' Homosexual-Men Detection Model Denounced as a Threat to LGBTQ People’s Safety and Privacy
AIID-167.summary: Researchers at Stanford developed a facial analysis model capable of predicting sexual orientation with high accuracy using dating profile photos. The study faced significant backlash from advocacy groups and academics who argued it was 'junk science' and posed severe safety and privacy risks to the LGBTQ community, particularly in regions where homosexuality is criminalized. The researchers stated the project was intended to highlight privacy vulnerabilities, but the resulting controversy led to death threats against the lead researcher.

AIID-169.title: Facebook Allegedly Failed to Police Anti-Rohingya Hate Speech Content That Contributed to Violence in Myanmar
AIID-169.summary: Facebook and WhatsApp were used as primary tools for spreading anti-Rohingya hate speech, dehumanizing propaganda, and fabricated news in Myanmar. This content, often orchestrated by the military and nationalist groups, incited real-world violence, including ethnic cleansing, displacement, and the assassination of prominent figures. Despite repeated warnings from researchers and NGOs, the platform failed to adequately police content or provide sufficient moderation resources in the local language, leading to significant human rights abuses.
AIID-169.description: Facebook allegedly did not adequately remove anti-Rohingya hate speech, some of which was extremely violent and dehumanizing, on its platform, contributing to the violence faced by Rohingya communities in Myanmar.

AIID-170.title: Target Suggested Maternity-Related Advertisements to a Teenage Girl's Home, Allegedly Correctly Predicting Her Pregnancy via Algorithm
AIID-170.summary: Target developed a predictive analytics model to identify pregnant customers based on their shopping habits to send targeted advertisements. The system gained notoriety after an anecdote surfaced about a father discovering his teenage daughter's pregnancy through targeted coupons sent by the retailer. While the accuracy and veracity of the specific anecdote have been debated, the incident highlights the privacy risks associated with corporate data mining and predictive modeling of sensitive personal life events.

AIID-172.title: NarxCare’s Risk Score Model Allegedly Lacked Validation and Trained on Data with High Risk of Bias
AIID-172.summary: NarxCare and AvertD are predictive algorithms used in the US healthcare system to assess opioid misuse risk. Critics and researchers argue these tools lack transparency, peer-reviewed validation, and are prone to bias against vulnerable populations, leading to the unjust denial of pain medication and the stigmatization of patients.
AIID-172.description: NarxCare's overdose risk algorithm, lacking peer-reviewed validation, uses sensitive data like doctor visits, prescriptions, and possibly genetic information, leading to significant biases against women and Black patients. Factors like sexual abuse and criminal records exacerbate stigmas and disparities, often resulting in unjust denial of necessary pain medication. The newly approved AvertD genetic test shares similar issues, further complicating and potentially harming medical treatment decisions.

AIID-173.title: AI Tools Failed to Sufficiently Predict COVID Patients, Some Potentially Harmful
AIID-173.summary: During the COVID-19 pandemic, hundreds of AI-based diagnostic and triage tools were developed and deployed in clinical settings. Multiple large-scale studies, including reviews by the Turing Institute and researchers at Maastricht University and the University of Cambridge, concluded that none of these tools were fit for clinical use due to poor data quality, flawed training methodologies, and lack of clinical validation. Experts expressed significant concern that these tools, some of which were marketed to hospitals, may have caused patient harm by providing inaccurate diagnostic information.

AIID-174.title: Fake LinkedIn Profiles Created Using GAN Photos
AIID-174.summary: Researchers at the Stanford Internet Observatory identified over 1,000 inauthentic LinkedIn profiles utilizing AI-generated headshots created via Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). These profiles were used by third-party lead-generation vendors to conduct automated sales outreach on behalf of various companies, including RingCentral, without the companies' explicit knowledge or authorization. LinkedIn subsequently removed the identified profiles for violating policies against fake accounts and falsified information.
AIID-174.description: More than a thousand inauthentic LinkedIn profiles using allegedly GAN-generated photos were notified by researchers at Stanford to LinkedIn’s staff, and many of which were removed for violating rules against creating fake profiles and falsifying information.

AIID-179.title: DALL-E 2 Reported for Gender and Racially Biased Outputs
AIID-179.summary: OpenAI's DALL-E 2 model was found to exhibit significant gender and racial biases, reinforcing societal stereotypes in its generated images. Researchers and internal audits confirmed that the model disproportionately associated certain professions with specific genders and races. In response, OpenAI implemented system-level prompt modifications to increase diversity, a move criticized by some experts as a non-transparent 'sticking plaster' that fails to address the underlying cultural biases in the training data.

AIID-180.title: Algorithm Used by the Malaysian Judiciary Reportedly Recommended Unusually High Sentencing to a Drug Possession Case
AIID-180.summary: The Malaysian judiciary piloted an AI sentencing tool in Sabah and Sarawak to provide recommendations for drug possession and rape cases. The system, developed by Sarawak Information Systems, faced legal challenges from defense lawyers who argued that its use was unconstitutional and that it lacked transparency. Concerns were raised regarding the potential for the algorithm to amplify bias and the risk of magistrates relying too heavily on machine-generated recommendations instead of exercising independent judicial discretion.
AIID-180.description: The AI system used by the Malaysian judiciary which explicitly considered age, employment, and socio-economic data provided sentencing to a drug possession case that was alleged by lawyer to be disproportionately high for the crime committed.

AIID-184.title: Facial Recognition Program in São Paulo Metro Stations Suspended for Illegal and Disproportionate Violation of Citizens’ Right to Privacy
AIID-184.summary: A court in São Paulo ordered the suspension of a facial recognition system, SecurOS, deployed in the city's metro stations. The ruling followed a lawsuit by civil society organizations arguing that the mass collection of biometric data from 4 million daily users was illegal, disproportionate, and lacked transparency or proper risk assessment. The metro operator, ViaQuatro, was ordered to halt the system's deployment and face daily fines for non-compliance.
AIID-184.description: A facial recognition program rolled out by São Paulo Metro Stations was suspended following a court ruling in response to a lawsuit by civil society organizations, who cited fear of it being integrated with other electronic surveillance entities without consent, and lack of transparency about the biometric data collection process of metro users.

AIID-185.title: TikTok's "For You" Algorithm Directed New Users towards Disinformation about the War in Ukraine
AIID-185.summary: An investigation by NewsGuard found that TikTok's 'For You' recommendation algorithm actively promoted disinformation regarding the Russia-Ukraine war to new users within 40 minutes of account creation. The algorithm, which prioritizes engagement, failed to distinguish between reliable news and false propaganda, such as manipulated video game footage and debunked Kremlin narratives. AIID-186.title: Algorithm Assessing Risk Faced by Victims of Gender Violence Misclassified Low-Risk Cases, Allegedly Leading to Homicide of Women and Children in Spain
AIID-186.summary: VioGén is a Spanish police algorithm designed to assess recidivism risk in gender violence cases. External audits and reports indicate that the system frequently underestimates risk, often assigning 'low' or 'no risk' scores to victims who are subsequently murdered. The system's performance is criticized for lack of transparency, reliance on rigid questionnaires, and the influence of available police resources on risk classification, leading to systemic failures in protecting vulnerable individuals.
AIID-186.description: In Spain, the algorithm that assesses recidivism risk in gender violence, VioGén, have critically underestimated the level of risk in a series of cases that ended in homicide of women and children since its first deployment.

AIID-188.title: Argentinian City Government Deployed Teenage-Pregnancy Predictive Algorithm Using Invasive Demographic Data
AIID-188.summary: In 2018, the Salta provincial government in Argentina, in partnership with Microsoft, deployed an AI system to predict teenage pregnancies among low-income and marginalized populations. The system utilized invasive personal data, including home infrastructure and disability status, and was criticized by activists and researchers for methodological flaws, lack of transparency, and potential for discriminatory surveillance and eugenic-style population control.
AIID-188.description: In 2018, during the abortion-decriminalization debate in Argentina, the Salta city government deployed a teenage-pregnancy predictive algorithm built by Microsoft that allegedly lacked a defined purpose, explicitly considered sensitive information such as disability and whether their home had access to hot water.

AIID-189.title: Opaque Fraud Detection Algorithm by the UK’s Department of Work and Pensions Allegedly Discriminated against People with Disabilities
AIID-189.summary: The UK Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) has been accused of using opaque, potentially discriminatory algorithms to flag benefit claimants for fraud investigations. Disability advocacy groups, including the Greater Manchester Coalition of Disabled People, report that these automated processes disproportionately target disabled individuals, subjecting them to invasive surveillance and bureaucratic hardship. The DWP maintains that human oversight is involved in all final decisions, but has refused to disclose the specific logic or bias-mitigation strategies of its fraud-detection systems.
AIID-189.description: People with disabilities were allegedly disproportionately targeted by a benefit fraud detection algorithm which the UK’s Department of Work and Pensions was urged to disclose.

AIID-191.title: Korean Internet Portal Giant Naver Manipulated Shopping and Video Search Algorithms to Favor In-House Services
AIID-191.summary: The Korean Fair Trade Commission (FTC) fined internet portal giant Naver 26.7 billion KRW for manipulating its search algorithms between 2012 and 2015. This practice misled consumers regarding the objectivity of search results and harmed fair competition in the South Korean e-commerce market.

AIID-193.title: Excessive Automated Monitoring Alerts Ignored by Staff, Resulting in Private Data Theft of Seventy Million Target Customers
AIID-193.summary: In 2013, Target suffered a massive data breach resulting in the theft of private data for 70 million customers. The breach went undetected by staff because the automated monitoring system (FireEye) generated a high volume of false positives, leading staff to ignore alerts or disable the system entirely. This incident highlights the critical issue of alert fatigue in security operations and the necessity for context-aware, prioritized security analytics.
AIID-193.description: Alerts about a Target data breach were ignored by Minneapolis Target’s staff reportedly due to them being included with many other potential false alerts, and due to some of the company’s network infiltration alerting systems being off to reduce such false alerts, causing private data theft for millions of customers.
AIID-193.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"2.1 Compromise of privacy by obtaining, leaking or correctly inferring sensitive information","justification":"The failure of the monitoring system directly enabled a massive data breach where the private data of 70 million customers was stolen."}]

AIID-193.aiGoalJustification: The FireEye system's primary function was to monitor network and user activity data to detect anomalies and alert security staff of potential malicious events.

The system failed to accurately assess incident scenarios, leading to excessive technician dispatches and significant financial waste. Due to a lack of a 'kill switch' or manual override capability, the company was forced to spend millions on a year-long fix-up project while the flawed system remained in operation.

AIID-195.title: Predictive Policing Program by Florida Sheriff’s Office Allegedly Violated Residents’ Rights and Targeted Children of Vulnerable Groups
AIID-195.summary: The Pasco County Sheriff’s Office implemented an 'Intelligence-Led Policing' program that used an algorithm to identify and target residents, including minors, for aggressive surveillance. The system utilized sensitive school and child welfare data to label individuals as potential future criminals, leading to systematic harassment, unwarranted home visits, and retaliatory arrests. The program has been widely criticized by experts as discriminatory and a violation of civil rights.
AIID-195.description: The Intelligence-Led Policing model rolled out by the Pasco County Sheriff’s Office was allegedly developed based on flawed science and biased data that also contained sensitive information and irrelevant attributes about students, which critics said to be discriminatory.

AIID-196.title: Compromise of National Biometric ID Card System Leads to Reverification and Change of Status
AIID-196.summary: The Pakistani National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) implemented a biometric identification system that, while intended to improve service delivery and security, has caused widespread harm. Automated rules within the system have led to the mass suspension of hundreds of thousands of national identity cards (CNICs), effectively rendering citizens stateless and denying them access to basic rights, welfare, and financial services. Courts have repeatedly ruled that NADRA's automated adjudication of family and paternity disputes is illegal and lacks jurisdiction.
AIID-196.description: When the leader of the Afghan Taliban was found possessing a valid ID card in the Pakistani national biometric identification database system, Pakistan launch a national re-verification campaign that is linked to numerous changes in recognition status and loss of services.

AIID-197.title: Facebook Internally Reported Failure of Ranking Algorithm, Exposing Harmful Content to Viewers over Months
AIID-197.summary: A software bug in Facebook's ranking algorithm, active for approximately six months between October 2021 and March 2022, caused the system to fail to downrank harmful content. This resulted in increased visibility for misinformation, nudity, violence, and Russian state media, with some posts seeing a 30% spike in views. Meta acknowledged the issue as a 'level-one site event' but maintained that it did not have a meaningful long-term impact on its metrics.
AIID-197.description: Facebook's internal report showed an at-least six-month long alleged software bug that caused moderator-flagged posts and other harmful content to evade down-ranking filters, leading to surges of misinformation on users' News Feed.
AIID-197.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"3.1 False or misleading information","justification":"The ranking failure directly led to a massive surge of misinformation being boosted to users instead of being demoted."},{"code":"1.2 Exposure to toxic content","justification":"The system failed to properly demote nudity and violence, exposing users to potentially toxic and inappropriate content."}]
AIID-197.domainJustification: The incident was primarily caused by a software bug in the ranking algorithm that led to a massive system failure, demonstrating a lack of robustness in critical content moderation functions.
AIID-197.modelName: Meta Facebook News Feed Ranking Algorithm
AIID-197.aiGoalJustification: The primary function of the Facebook News Feed algorithm is to recommend and rank content for users, while a key secondary function is moderating that content by downranking integrity risks.

AIID-198.title: Deepfake Video of Ukrainian President Yielding to Russia Posted on Ukrainian Websites and Social Media
AIID-198.summary: On March 16, 2022, a deepfake video of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy was circulated online, falsely showing him calling for his country to surrender to Russian forces. The video was also broadcast on the hacked news channel Ukraine 24. The incident was quickly debunked by the Ukrainian government and removed by major social media platforms, but it highlighted the potential for AI-generated disinformation to be used as a weapon in armed conflict.
AIID-198.description: A quickly-debunked deepfaked video of the Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy was posted on various Ukrainian websites and social media platforms encouraging Ukrainians to surrender to Russian forces during the Russia-Ukraine war.

AIID-199.title: Ever AI Reportedly Deceived Customers about FRT Use in App
AIID-199.summary: Everalbum, a photo storage app, deceived millions of users by using their uploaded photos to train facial recognition models without informed consent. The company then marketed this technology to enterprise clients, including law enforcement and military agencies. Following an FTC investigation, the company was ordered to delete the illegally trained models and algorithms and to obtain express consent for future biometric data usage.
AIID-199.description: Ever AI, now Paravision AI, allegedly failed to inform customers about the development and use of facial recognition that facilitates the sale of customers’ data to various businesses, a business model that critics said was an egregious violation of privacy.
AIID-199.subdomain: 2.1 Compromise of privacy by obtaining, leaking or correctly inferring sensitive information
AIID-199.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"4.1 Disinformation, surveillance, and influence at scale","justification":"The harvested data was used to develop and train facial recognition models marketed to law enforcement and military for surveillance purposes."}]
AIID-199.domainJustification: The company extracted biometric face embeddings and trained facial recognition models using private, non-public photos uploaded by users to a cloud storage app without their consent.
AIID-199.aiGoalJustification: The primary purpose of the Ever AI system was to perform facial recognition and matching, which was also used in the consumer app for grouping and tagging photos.

AIID-200.title: Fraudsters Used AI to Mimic Voice of a UK-Based Firm's CEO's Boss
AIID-200.summary: In March 2019, fraudsters used AI-based voice synthesis software to impersonate the CEO of a German parent company, successfully deceiving a UK-based subsidiary executive into transferring €220,000 to a fraudulent account. The attackers attempted a second transfer later that day, but the victim became suspicious due to the caller's use of an Austrian phone number. This incident is cited as one of the first documented cases of cybercrime involving AI-driven voice spoofing.

AIID-203.title: Uber Launched Opaque Algorithm That Changes Drivers' Payments in the US
AIID-203.summary: Uber introduced an opaque 'Upfront Fares' algorithm in 24 U.S. cities to determine driver pay, replacing traditional time-and-distance calculations. Drivers have reported significant confusion, decreased earnings on long trips, and a lack of transparency regarding how the algorithm determines pay. Critics and researchers have raised concerns about the use of 'black box' algorithms in gig work, noting that the lack of clear criteria makes it difficult for drivers to verify fair compensation.
AIID-203.description: Uber launched a new but opaque algorithm to determine drivers' pay in the US which allegedly caused drivers to experience lower fares, confusing fare drops, and a decrease in rides.
